statements: Use nonmandatory, nonexhaustive discrimination techniques: invariance across multiple existing contexts; structurally similar but operationally distinct null peers; adjacent treatment and adjoint interpret-back preserving identity; transplant of identity requirements to a neighbour; coat stripping that preserves identity when context varies but not when identity claims vary.

grounding.quote:
Techniques
that serve this, none of them mandatory and none of them exhaustive:

- cross-context invariance: separate what holds wherever the entity
  appears from what a particular context adds, where multiple contexts
  exist;
- null-peer comparison: name a structurally similar entity the operating
  model treats differently, and state what separates them;
- adjoint round-trip: interpret the entity through an adjacent domain's
  treatment surface and back through its adjoint mapping, and show the
  identity claim survives;
- transplant: show what a neighbouring entity would have to acquire to be
  treated as this one;
- coat stripping: vary or remove contextual claims and show identity
  survives; vary an identity claim and show it does not.

statements: Projects choose different declared risk appetites and ambiguity policies.
Policy may permit bounded probabilistic carrying/decision or require escalation to admitted human adjudication.
Progressive reduction, rather than elimination of all ambiguity before work, is permitted.

grounding.quote:
The default governance model: ambiguity
may be carried or decided by lawful probabilistic processing when project
policy allows it; it may be escalated to explicit human adjudication when
project policy requires it; the threshold between those actions is
determined by declared risk appetite, not by silent convenience. Projects
may therefore choose different ambiguity-handling policies: a lower risk
appetite escalates more major ambiguity to explicit human judgment; a
higher one permits more bounded probabilistic decision-making. In either
case the ambiguity and the decision are recorded.

The hard stops of [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)
hold regardless of risk appetite. The method is therefore not "eliminate
all ambiguity before work"; it is "make ambiguity visible, govern it
explicitly, and reduce it progressively until downstream realisation is
sufficiently constrained".

conditions: Once the project has decided its outcomes and capabilities.

entropy, eliminate avoidable technical debt, increase refactorability,
reduce hidden authority, hidden mutation and semantic drift in realisation
code, and preserve enough evidence that later reviewers can audit,
refactor and reconstruct why the realisation took its current shape (P2,

traversal should have a finite, inspectable unit for reasoning,
implementation, evaluation, proof and later refactor. A module boundary is
one realisation-level tool for creating that unit; it is not the only
possible bounded traversal.

value.label: Decision-complete material-relation network
value.definition: M(B) is the complete material-relation network: entities; identities; relationships; cardinalities; invariants; authorities; authority transitions; functions; higher-order composition laws; topology; lifecycle states and transitions; public contracts; externally observable Product meaning; declared domains and admission conditions; failure and refusal routes; effect and closure laws; projections; module mappings; material algorithmic obligations. U(B) is its unresolved subset. Decision completeness requires empty U(B), joint satisfiability, and semantic equivalence of every admitted network under governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations. Co-evolution admissibility is exactly decision completeness. The design gate is the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish it.
conditions: B is one governed boundary.

grounding.quote:
U(B) = unresolved(M(B))
decision_complete(B) iff
  U(B) = empty
  and M(B) is jointly satisfiable
  and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under the
      governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations
co_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B)
design_gate(B) =
  the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish
  decision_complete(B)

M(B) =
  entities + identities + relationships + cardinalities + invariants
  + authorities + authority transitions + functions
  + higher-order composition laws + topology
  + lifecycle states and transitions + public contracts
  + externally observable Product meaning
  + declared domains and admission conditions
  + failure and refusal routes + effect and closure laws
  + projections + module mappings + material algorithmic obligations

  is not top-level by default;
- Promotion Test: the explicit test a Subordinate Payload passes before it
  becomes a top-level type; and
- Boundary Inflation: the defect where subordinate payload detail is
  promoted into extra peer types without irreducible need.

its authoritative inputs, together with what is justifiably known about

current state, not the state itself

Its three subject accounts are specification of required conditions, observations of what holds, and causal/predictive explanation of possible action effects. Strategy arranges admissible construction and assurance within resources; a composition boundary passes one step's output into the next starting state and differs from a categorical join. Feedback observes, compares, diagnoses, selects an authorized response, acts and observes again; homeostasis is correction toward required conditions without a convergence or adequacy guarantee.

selected construction binds its current state and destination, chooses
its work, composes its steps, corrects itself and claims completion. This
section owns that relation. ACTIVATION §2 to §7, EVALUATION §1,
SPEC_METHOD §4 and §8, EXECUTIVE_BASELINE and ODD apply it through their
local bindings; none creates a competing determination (P6).

value.label: Foundational ontology objects
value.definition: Ontology categories: Subject is the exact thing a claim, representation or transformation concerns, identified by inventory and bytes or semantic addresses. Representation is bytes, text, model or program standing for a subject. Interpretation is a declared context-bound representation-to-meaning contract identifying reliable distinctions and residuals. Context declares subject, definitions, basis and admissible observations. Outcome U is an owner-selected directly verifiable state with acceptance interval. Object O has scoped identity (authority, kind, value), boundary, state and material relations. Actor performs a step within context, attention, time and capability limits; role is an occupied relation selected by configuration. Step is bounded intake, selected context, grant, execution and output. Step-produced fact is a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision that cannot be reacquired from declared sources; reproducible observations are excluded. Claim binds subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier. Evidence comprises admitted exact observations/artifacts with provenance, subject identity, basis and scope. Judgment is recorded evaluation over unchanged subject, with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation. Authority is identity-bearing scoped permission to operate or dispose acceptance. Residual is material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation awaiting authorised disposition. Basis is every exact version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change can alter the bound step, claim, result or evaluation. Materiality is evaluation-relative potential to change result, basis validity, admissible evidence, operation performer or decision owner, including uncertainty and closure.

value.label: Reference-frame ontology
value.definition: Frame objects: Evaluation is a declared question with known result family, evidence basis, decision authority and material-operation authority where needed, admitting judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation. Evaluation family shares required manifold, authority basis and result algebra. Workspace is bounded reasoned-over or acted-on material, potentially broader than a repository. Material-relation manifold is the finite jointly interpretable variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions needed by a family, allowing overlapping coordinate charts without implied geometry or runtime. Coordinate is complete locally required basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority information. Topology is the material relation structure visible at one basis, not necessarily complete workspace topology. Capability envelope is required competence, context capacity, tools, access, independence and configuration. Reference frame specifies finite attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations for a family and basis. Activated frame binds declaration to exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary. Frame set is a human-declared available family permitting overlaps, alternatives, specialists, exploration and separate assurance. Active frame configuration is activations and declared result relations for one evaluation or decision. Lens is a reusable question family, becoming a frame only on full bounded instantiation. Role allocates responsibility/authority; persona changes approach/salience; abstraction hides/contracts detail; component is structural. None is a frame merely by identity.

grounding.quote:
The reference frame and the objects it binds are first-class in this
corpus.

value.label: P0–P6 commitments
value.definition: P0 Bounded construction is recovered: finite actors realise selected outer contracts through fitting steps, owning their internal path; actors may change and reacquire declared sources but not private memory, step-produced facts are not reacquirable, the world is open and output is candidate until evaluated. P1 Interpretation is independent: subject, representation and context-bound meaning differ; structural success is not fidelity and semantic decisions require exact contracts. P2 Purpose is independent: selected outcome defines adequacy and interface obligations derive from the served transformation. P3 Identity is independent: declared authority/kind/value identity survives admissible change and boundaries carry proof obligations. P4a Typed composition is independent: prior type and judgment must satisfy the next exact domain and preconditions, retaining identities, intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. P4b Conservation is derived from P0 and P2 plus non-reacquirability: producing steps record outer-contract-needed judgments, residuals, observations and authority decisions; reacquirable sources follow sufficiency rather than conservation. P5 Totality is derived from P0 and P6 plus open-world premise: no success on outside-context conditions, first-class non-success and named next moves. P6 Justification and authority is independent: definitions, assumptions, observations, candidate judgments and accepted claims have distinct standing; evidence supports basis-bound claims and authority permits or disposes only within scope.

value.label: Assertion provenance, execution provenance and authentication
value.definition: Assertion provenance comprises the owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies. Execution provenance comprises actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment, inputs, observations and result. Authentication binds a returned assessment to producer, subject, basis and evidence but establishes neither provenance. Construction and assurance may derive along different paths from a common obligation, such as requirement → refinement → realisation; these example roles prescribe no stage names or test classes.

grounding.quote:
An expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the
owning obligation, its interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared
dependencies, which give it meaning. An execution has execution
provenance: the actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment,
inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they
support; execution records alone cannot establish that the expected
answer follows from the requirement. Authentication of a returned
assessment, which binds a result to its producer, subject, basis and
evidence ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), is a
third thing and establishes neither provenance (P6, P3).

value.definition: Assertion justification explains why a check expresses an obligation; evidence validity identifies dependencies affecting behaviour, conclusion or applicability, including implementation, libraries, data, instruments, environments and governing assumptions. For a material change Δ, including discovery of an invalid assumption, I(Δ) conservatively covers changed facts and affected dependents; D*(t) covers transitive dependencies material to assertion, execution and evidence use. dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an
obligation. The latter identifies what can affect the check's behaviour,
conclusion or applicability: implementation, shared libraries, data,
instruments, environments and governing assumptions. A
requirements-to-test link alone is not a complete impact model (P3, P6).
E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.

value.label: Locator ownership, imports and staleness watch
value.definition: Every locus is an owning corpus clause. A concept's defining section supplies its owning clause, with context ownership supplied directly or by its member. Imported concepts cite the defining section and identify the importing declaration or stated owner relation in the relation clause; otherwise that clause only locates an externally stated relationship. A concept outside all bounded contexts declared by its member uses the member as source context; §16 indexes it without declaring a new context. An index watch separately records locator path and digest from deciding sources, and locator drift makes dependent surfaces or frames stale without making the index a meaning owner.

grounding.quote:
A concept defined outside every bounded context its member declares has
that member as its source context
([FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members)).
§16 indexes those concepts with the member in place of a bounded-context
identity. Such a row declares no context, and a context holds one of those
concepts only by its own import (P1, P3).

Index watch. A derived surface or projected frame that relies on this
index to locate meaning watches it through the index's path and digest,
recorded separately from the deciding sources it was derived from. Locator
drift in this index then makes that surface or frame stale
([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §11](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#11-one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary),
staleness binding), and the watch does not make this index an owner of
meaning (P3, P6).

value.label: Frame configuration
value.definition: A configuration allocates task responsibilities and information exchanges to frames across the work; activation binds actors to frames. An active frame configuration is the portion used for one evaluation or decision. A coordinator, where selected, manages delivery across tasks from bounded closed results. The optional Executive configuration assigns construction to Worker/Writer, assessment to Reviewer, and longer-term outcome, next-work selection and granted disposition to a non-mutating Executive; it is not the method default.

grounding.quote:
A configuration allocates a task's responsibilities and information
exchanges to frames; activation binds an actor to each frame (§2). It
spans the task's work. The active frame configuration of
[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects) is the part of it used for
one evaluation or decision (P0, P6).

It allocates construction,
assessment and disposition (Roles and delegation below) to three frames: a
Worker frame, specialised as Writer for documents and records, constructs;
a Reviewer frame assesses; an Executive frame keeps the longer-term
outcome, selects the next work and disposes within its decision grant, and
mutates nothing. That profile owns its frames, their grants, limits and
prohibitions, and its explanation; they apply where it is selected. It is
not the method's default. A configuration with other frames, names or
topology is evaluated as Evaluation of a configuration above states.

value.definition: Tier 3 Outcome-Driven Development profile for graph-native product authoring over a declared asset graph. It owns graph-native terms in urn:stdo:bounded-context:graph-native-odd under the selected complete STDO basis, imports listed families by reference and restates none. grounding.quote:
This profile's graph traversal and its F_D, F_P and F_H shorthands are its
own concepts and are not those records by spelling. The Executive, Worker
and Reviewer of [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md) are roles, and roles
are relations over steps in which no role name confers an operation
([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)); the actor, the
executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are different
coordinates (AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5) (P3, P6).

This profile owns those concepts in the graph-native bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:graph-native-odd` under the selected complete
STDO basis. The context covers the ODD product shape, the GTL language
role, the ABG method role, graph assets, vectors, functions, traversals and
the graph and runtime worker and evaluator shorthands defined here. It does

reusable starter forms and examples and are convenience artifacts only.

value.label: Responsibility layer
value.definition: A structural responsibility layer expresses one capability class, which the product binds to local domain semantics and the GTL carrier exposes through lawful transitions. Examples are bootstrap/intake, design, implementation, qualification, release, operational transition and retrofit; they are not mandatory instance names.

grounding.quote:
This profile governs structural responsibility layers and their required
publication shape. It does not freeze one product's local asset names as
universal ODD doctrine. A responsibility layer expresses one capability
class; the product binds that capability to its own local domain
semantics; the GTL carrier publishes the lawful transitions for that bound
capability (P1, P3).

Capability classes may include bootstrap or intake, design,
implementation, qualification, release, operational transition and
retrofit. They are responsibility-layer ideas, not mandatory universal
instance names (P1).

value.label: Constructive loop carriers
value.definition: Loop carrier vocabulary: IntentLineage is admitted source intent and lineage from a human, imported source, prior product, intent engine or prior synthesized construction intent, backed by ABG event-log truth. ProductAssetModel is desired and known typed asset truth synthesized from lineage, prior model and admitted product truth, with admitted-event and product-projection publication refs; it is neither runtime fact nor action authority. Worksite is the observable workspace, runtime archive, transform assets, product asset root, profile and file/process state. RuntimeEventLog is append-only admitted runtime facts; RuntimeProjection is replay-derived runtime state over event log and execution basis. ObservationSnapshot is a read-only runtime/worksite view; GapPressureRow represents missing, partial, blocked, waiting or ambiguous asset/evidence pressure. TargetObligationBinding binds pressure to the exact selected outcome, admitted prerequisite/experiment basis, assets, roles, evidence and admissible outcomes. ActionCatalog publishes lawful graph functions, vectors, targets, inputs and eligible outcomes. NextActionBasis is the dispatch sum initial_selection, post_yield_resume, post_close_graph_continuation, post_retry, post_repair, post_reenter, post_reprice or post_block, not a controller. PriorityProjection deterministically ranks bound lawful actions under visible policy. ConstructionIntent is an admitted selected action for one bounded invocation preserving outcome/basis refs. AdmittedEvidence includes worker, process, product, execution, materialization, liveness and postflight evidence, without worker self-closure. EdgeFulfillmentLedger carries evidence and convergence for one edge attempt/version. EdgeClosureDecision carries closure truth. NextActionProjection reads current truth and NextActionBasis and selects only when lawful.
exceptions: post_reprice carries a re-entry request and no action-selection authority.

grounding.quote: | `NextActionProjection` | Read model that observes `NextActionBasis` plus current truth and selects a next graph action only when lawful. | ABG next-action evaluation projection with product policy. |

| `TargetObligationBinding` | Exact binding from gap pressure to the selected Product outcome, any admitted prerequisite or experiment basis, target assets, required roles, evidence refs, and admissible graph outcomes. | Product domain binding over GTL/ABG action authority. |

value.definition: Four owner-authorized cross-context relation kinds: Semantic Import applies unchanged source meaning in declared target scope under FOUNDATIONS import law; Semantic Translation declares directional meaning change and loss and is not an import; Semantic Equivalence is an equality established by governing authorities while both concepts retain owners/contexts and neither adopts the other's meaning; Semantic Disambiguation selects one meaning for one scope without equating alternatives, using a declared import/translation/equivalence if the selected meaning is external. Specialisation is directional translation preserving declared source meaning while narrowing admissible instances or adding target constraints.

grounding.quote:
A specialisation is a directional translation whose target preserves the
declared source meaning while narrowing its admissible instances or adding
target-context constraints. It identifies the exact target concept, the
preserved and narrowed meaning, the excluded source instances, and the
absence or law of any inverse. Calling a term a specialisation without
those coordinates establishes nothing (P1, P3).

value.label: WHAT, tenant registry and work-carrier bindings
value.definition: Tenant Registry is canonical how.build_tenants, identifying independent HOW realizations by stable identity and locating roots/design/implementation; tenant surfaces declare bindings under SPEC_METHOD §11. how.common locates common realization law explicitly adopted across multiple tenants. WHAT bindings locate current Intent, Product and specifications. ticketing.goals locates the work wave; ticketing.tickets locates durable tickets with backlog/active/completed lanes; ticketing.comments locates commentary; optional ticketing.sprints locates bounded execution-batch manifests.

grounding.quote:
The Tenant Registry is the canonical `how.build_tenants` collection for the
product's independent HOW realisations. Each entry has stable identity and
locates its root, design and implementation surfaces; the tenant's
binding, which those surfaces declare, is governed by SPEC_METHOD §11.
The Common Build-Tenant Surface is the realisation law bound by `how.common` and
explicitly adopted across more than one tenant. A separate
`TENANT_REGISTRY.md` may remain as a human-readable companion or generated
projection and cannot become a second tenant-identity or location
authority (P3, P6).

grounding.quote:
The reference frame is the atomic engagement unit: the unit that is
activated and evaluated as one bounded context. Frame-set selection,
activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision are
separate functions over it (§5). A frame supports a bounded evaluation
without first containing a universal theory of its possible relationships.

relation inside the frame is one irreducible semantic atom; a frame may
carry several semantic atoms and several owner relations without merging
their meaning or authority (P1, P3).

grounding.quote:
Every performed evaluation of a frame returns one closed result in the
frame's declared result algebra: the core algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), or a refinement mapped
into it under that section. That section owns the five core values
(`satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`, `out_of_frame` and
`invalid_basis`), their meanings and the rules over them: that nothing is
coerced to success; that a refinement adds no core value, keeps
indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure explicit and raises
no result's standing; and that an evaluation not performed has no result,
its stop state being
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition). This law
applies them to every frame and defines none of them (P5).

value.label: Specification-driven method
value.definition: Specification-driven development is a governed derivation and disambiguation method: current goals precede deeper repricing, intent precedes implementation, product definition precedes detailed requirements, and design explicitly bridges requirements to code.

grounding.quote:
The method commits to these (P2, P6). It defines the
current goals for the active body of work before repricing deeper
constitutional layers. It works from intent before implementation. It
defines the current product definition in explicit present-tense terms
before decomposing it into detailed requirements. It defines the full
constitutional what in requirements, not merely a feature list. It prefers
declaring desired truth and lawful boundaries over prescribing step-by-step
imperative procedure. It makes design the explicit structural bridge
between requirements and code. It requires code to be derivable from
requirements and design, not defended as accidental precedent. It treats
spec-driven development as a disambiguation pipeline: each major gate
reduces the space of lawful interpretations before downstream realisation
proceeds.

value.label: Requirement classifications
value.definition: Requirement category and lifecycle status are independent declared-state domains. Categories are Capability (required behaviour/function/surface), Constraint / Guarantee (invariant, law, safety, portability or semantic bound), Governance (lifecycle, authority, visibility, release or operator policy), and Verification (tests, evidence, traceability, qualification or forensic obligations). grounding.quote:
| Capability | a behaviour, function or surface the system must provide | what can the system do |
| Constraint / Guarantee | an invariant, law, safety property, portability rule or semantic guarantee that bounds how the system may behave | what must always remain true |
| Governance | a policy or control rule over lifecycle, authority, visibility, release or operator action | what governs use and change |
| Verification | a requirement on tests, evidence, traceability, qualification or forensic surfaces | how do we know the claim is true |

Every live requirement family is classified on two independent axes (P3,
P1): lifecycle status (Active,
Deferred, Superseded, Orphaned) and requirement category (the four above).

preservation and regression. The four refine the progress

proof, useful evidence, not progress; regression maps to evidence that

ACTIVATION §5's, unchanged here.

value.label: F11 foundation-to-law family
value.definition: F11 is the foundation-to-law family accounting for change entry, computed classification and reuse, ambiguity governance and shared-interface migration. Its instance premises are changing specification, one front door, shared interfaces with multiple producers/consumers, and decisions either under declared policy or reserved to human authority. It reports P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts; and P5 derived from P0/P6 with an open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
This family (F11 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law))
decides how a change enters the chain, how its classification is computed
and reused, how ambiguity is governed and how a shared interface is
migrated. Its instance premises, which the commitments do not supply, are
named in the rows as follows: changing specification, the specification
changes while work proceeds; one front door, reports of every kind arrive
at one product; shared interfaces, a shared interface has several
producers and consumers; reserved decisions, a decision may be taken
under declared policy or be reserved to a human authority. Standing of
the commitments cited (FOUNDATIONS §3): P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and
P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2, with P0's premise that
step-produced facts are not re-acquirable; P5 derived from P0 and P6,
with P0's open-world premise.

value.label: Lineage and release identities
value.definition: Lineage distinguishes substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition. A release cut v<version>-rc.<n> is immutable point-in-time release identity; mutable v<version> is a discovery selector for the highest-ordinal published cut.

grounding.quote:
The roles are distinct objects with distinct identities,
substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product,
install, artifact and product definition, defined once in FOUNDATIONS §2
(product lineage objects) with their governing rules and the compiler
analogy; the product definition is the source project's present-tense
surface, not the released artifact and not the builder that happens to be
running the build (P3).

The only exact operative release identifier is the immutable release-cut
tag `v<version>-rc.<n>` (P3). That cut is a
point-in-time release identity, a boundary over the feature set accepted
for that cut, and part of release metadata and release-process evaluation;
it is not part of the live project specification. The mutable `v<version>`
tag is a version-line discovery selector to the highest-ordinal published
immutable cut; it is not an exact dependency, evidence or constitutional
basis and cannot silently change a consumer selection.

value.label: Constitutional migration strategies
value.definition: Two lawful strategies are inside-out hard-break migration on the same implementation line, replacing authoritative source truth from its carrier outward, and fundamental re-adoption for intentional major re-derivation on a materially different implementation basis. Bounded evolution is a rebuttable selection presumption, not a third strategy.

grounding.quote:
Core interface and major implementation replacement work has two lawful
constitutional strategies (P3, P6).
Inside-out hard-break migration applies when the project remains on the
same implementation line and the authoritative source truth is being
replaced in place; the work proceeds from the source carrier outward
through a sequence of deliberate breaks and repairs. Fundamental
re-adoption migration applies when the rewrite is major and the project is
intentionally re-deriving itself on a materially different implementation
basis, such as a new runtime model, carrier model, type system, execution
substrate or realisation tree; the prior implementation is moved sideways
and treated as reference material, not live authority.

grounding.quote:
Refactor and migration should be understood as a transformation wave over
mutable
implementation surfaces (P3, P6). While
the wave is in flight: temporary mixed-state implementation may exist only
below the current break boundary and only as explicitly non-authoritative
plumbing; transitional adapters or scaffolds may exist only when they are
named, bounded and outside the acceptance path; refactor state may still
carry traces of the prior operative model, never as competing or ambiguous
dual authority over the same request, fact, identity, state or projection.
Explicitly specified, deterministically routed, non-overlapping product or
compatibility scopes are not competing authority under this rule; they may
coexist while the enclosing migration remains visibly open.

value.label: Architecture decision record
value.definition: An ADR is durable design memory per decision boundary: the choice making acceptance criteria true. Its declared statuses are active, superseded and retired; it is an authoritative design file, while templates and optional registries project its rules.

grounding.quote:
Each ADR explicitly includes `Status:` (`active`, `superseded` or
`retired`); `Implements:` (the requirement identifiers the ADR makes true);
`Derives from:` (the intent identifier or strategy document that motivated
the decision); `Supersedes:` (the prior ADR or doctrine it replaces);
`Superseded by:` (the successor ADR when its status is superseded); and
`Retained special case:` (when earlier behaviour is intentionally retained
as a special case of the current surface) (P6, P4b).
ADRs are written per decision boundary, not per requirement file; the
boundary is the question "what design choice makes these acceptance
criteria true".

value.label: TICKETS sprint manifest
value.definition: In TICKETS, a sprint is one bounded-batch manifest under optional ticketing.sprints.root, default .ai-workspace/sprints/, batching authority references, closure law, evidence expectations and deferred local compliance debt and closing by explicit review.

grounding.quote:
Sprints are bounded execution batches. Each sprint is one manifest under
the product definition's optional `ticketing.sprints.root` binding,
`.ai-workspace/sprints/` being the default; a control surface for a bounded
body of work; a place to batch repeated authority references, closure law,
evidence expectations and deferred local compliance debt; and closed by an
explicit sprint-close review. Sprints are not constitutional authority: they
operate under SPEC_METHOD and the project surfaces they cite
([SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#sprint-execution-boundary) states the
sprint boundary; this member states the mechanics) (P2, P6).

value.label: Comment carrier
value.definition: Comments are POSTING_GUIDE posts for ideas, strategy, reviews, handoffs, closure summaries and reasoned decisions, located by ticketing.comments.root with .ai-workspace/comments/ as default. They have neither task-status authority nor independent decision authority.

grounding.quote:
The product definition's `ticketing.comments.root` binding is the message
board; `.ai-workspace/comments/` is the default. Comments are for publishing
ideas, strategy notes, reviews, handoffs, closure summaries, and decisions
with their reasoning. Comments are not task status authority. A comment
is a post of [POSTING_GUIDE](POSTING_GUIDE.md), which states what it
carries, its structure and its discussion state. A decision recorded in a
comment takes its authority from the surface that owns the decision, once
it is adopted there ([POSTING_GUIDE §9](POSTING_GUIDE.md#9-ratification)),
and has none of its own (P6, P3).

value.label: Markov Object
value.definition: Load-bearing candidate construct: a stable self-bounding pattern in a constraint structure, with internal state reasoned about through an effective blanket. Its substrate-neutral propagation across biology, language traces, learned representations and engineered institutions is a working claim. Published Markov-object language denotes an immutable ledger-derived cut with identity direction and distributed evidence, while recovered entities can be published as entity cuts independently.

grounding.quote:
A Markov object is
a stable self-bounding pattern in a constraint structure whose internal
state can be reasoned about through its effective blanket. The term is
substrate-neutral: the same topology is expected wherever a constraint
structure admits stable configurations, in biological systems, in the natural-language traces those systems emit, in
learned representations built over those traces (LLMs), and in the
engineered institutional systems descended from both. The working claim
is that world-model construction is possible because this topology
propagates across substrates: what domain experts recognise as "objects"
in an institutional system is the same kind of stable constraint
structure hypothesised for biological systems, re-expressed through
another substrate.

The
published Markov object is an immutable object cut projected from the
attribute ledger, not an in-place mutable record; the cut is an identity
direction together with the distributed attribute evidence that supports
it, not an enumeration of member columns (P3, P4b).

value.definition: The sole constitutional semantic truth surface consists of published domain artifacts, bounded fragments, entity cuts, explicit treatments, covariance edges, adjoint mappings, temporal reference artifacts and models composed by reference. Epistemic overlays, query planes, mapping reports and compiled execution artifacts are downstream or supporting.

grounding.quote:
World-model work has one constitutional truth surface: the published
semantic layer (P6). That layer consists of
published domain artifacts; their bounded fragments and published entity
cuts; explicit treatments, covariance edges, adjoint mappings and
temporal reference artifacts; and composed world models built by
reference from those published artifacts. Everything else is downstream
or supporting: epistemic overlays, query planes, mapping reports and
compiled deterministic execution artifacts. Those surfaces may be

value.label: Control plane and data plane
value.definition: Semantic control plane contains published artifacts, composed models, treatments, covariance edges, adjoint mappings and epistemic overlays. The high-volume data plane contains deterministic executable artifacts compiled from accepted semantic understanding. The split distinguishes truth, probabilistic correspondence and runtime behaviour without creating another truth surface.

grounding.quote:
The semantic
control plane consists of published domain artifacts; composed world
models; treatments, covariance edges and adjoint mappings; and epistemic
overlays for correspondence, ranking and ambiguity. The high-volume data
plane consists of deterministic executable artifacts compiled from
accepted semantic understanding. That means: world-model artifacts carry
semantic truth; epistemic overlays carry probabilistic correspondence and
uncertainty; compiled execution artifacts carry deterministic runtime
behaviour. This is a plane split, not a truth split; the semantic truth
surface remains the published world-model layer (§3 Single truth
surface) (P6).

grounding.quote:
Each refinement names
the question it answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps
each of its values to exactly one core value. The predicate travels with
the value, so a `satisfied` for one predicate never counts toward another
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),
and no mapping raises a result's standing: nothing is coerced to
`satisfied` (P5, P6).

value.label: End-to-end interface integration refinement
value.definition: Composite refinement urn:stdo:reference-frame:end-to-end-interface-integration:v1, resolving in urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation owned by REFERENCE_FRAME. It relates public-boundary, design, operator, owner and proof evaluation to integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance frames. It asks whether one outcome remains constructable, understandable and correctly realised across its material interface chain with sufficient context and conserved meaning, authority and cause. Design subjects bind declared roles, functional paths, dependencies, configuration and capabilities; realisation subjects bind actual participants, callable selection, supported entry/exit and exact runnable artifact/install. Both bind an independent oracle, requirements/design, exact source/workspace checkpoint, contracts and finite cases. The manifold covers producers, consumers, transformations and effect owners, seam pre/postconditions, value/reference domains, lifecycle/time, context, mutable subject, refusals, observations and visible results. Coordinates distinguish Product, artifact/install, workspace, observation, invocation, candidate, admitted result and evidence, including revisions, domains, units, cardinality, ordering, empty/null/default meaning and validity intervals.
conditions: Selected by governing frame configuration or admitted work authority under the exact selected basis.

composite refinement whose identity resolves in
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation` (owned by
REFERENCE_FRAME) under the exact selected basis; its assurance law is
stated here. It relates the evaluation of public boundaries, design,
operators, owners and proof to the integration, end-to-end and
user-acceptance frames of §7. Like the set, it is available and is
activated only where the governing frame configuration or admitted work
authority selects it. It adds no fifth testing type, role or
universal activation gate (P2, P3).

value.definition: Four distinct claims: contract sufficiency asks whether every participant can determine and perform its responsibility from declared interfaces/context; boundary congruence asks whether actual selected producers, transformations and consumers preserve domains, meanings, lifecycle and authority; path realisation asks whether the exact runnable subject uses the authoritative entry-to-outcome path; user usability asks whether the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtains the outcome using only declared context, access and supported surfaces.

grounding.quote:
| contract sufficiency | Can each participant determine and perform its responsibility from the declared interface and the available context? Source-grounded design evaluation may establish this claim without an implemented runtime; unresolved realisability or actor-context questions stay explicit. |
| boundary congruence | Do the actual selected producers, transformations and consumers preserve the declared domains, meanings, lifecycle and authority? An actual-composition claim acquires both sides and their exchanges; design correspondence alone proves no implementation behaviour. |
| path realisation | Does the exact runnable subject use the authoritative entry-to-outcome path through its material state, effect and observation boundaries? Matching output through another path is insufficient. |
| user usability | Can the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtain the selected outcome using only its declared context, access and supported surface? Internal success or validator-aware fixtures cannot establish this claim. |

material) and the core result algebra of

[FOUNDATIONS §1](FOUNDATIONS.md#1-vocabulary-of-standing) requires.

for representing and relating governed symbolic systems. Its stable

owns that concept in the bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus`. Both identifiers are
declared identities and do not change with the carrier or the directory
that publishes them (P3).

value.label: Foundation-to-law account
value.definition: Material family F9's premise-to-rule account distinguishes derived consequences from owner-selected choices. Instance premises, not supplied by commitments, are: a finite model represents governed objects/relations/constraints/residuals/traversals/transformations/judgments; exact subject, interpreted model and possible carrier have separate identities; some predicates are mechanical and others need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication. P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are marked independent; P0 recovered; P4b derived from P0/P2; P5 derived from P0/P6. Nineteen rows bind these premises to position, scope, signature, identity/typing, authority/basis, results, latitude, residuals, closure/projection, overlay, transformation, judgment separation, traversal/composition, interpretation, layers, identity issuance, application/import boundaries, constraint surfaces and qualification.

grounding.quote:
This member is material family F9, the `a_c` calculus. The table below
shows which of its rules follow from which premises, in the format of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),
which also states the standing of the consequences. Instance premises,
which the commitments do not supply:

- (i) a governed symbolic system is represented by a finite model whose
  records stand for its objects, relations, constraints, residuals,
  traversals, transformations and judgments;
- (ii) a model is interpreted from an exact subject and may be encoded in
  a carrier, and subject, model and carrier are separately identified;
- (iii) some predicates over a model are decided mechanically, and others
  need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication.

value.label: Subject a_c model
value.definition: M_b = (b, I, O, E, C, L, X, V, T, J), with exact basis b, closed identity universe I and finite populations for semantic objects, directed relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals, transformations and judgments. Population_M is total over the eight core kinds. Local_M is their disjoint union; I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M. RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind, field) yields cardinality, allowed local kinds, semantic-object sorts, external target kinds and required basis relation.

grounding.quote:
`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population
is finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and
record identities are unique across their disjoint union. Let `Local_M` be
that union. Then `I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M`, where every
member of `External_M` is admitted only through one signature-declared
external reference domain and exact resolution relation. A hidden record,
an unpopulated extra record family, an identity occurring in two
populations, or an identity in `I` with neither one local record nor one
lawful external resolution refuses the model. A population may be empty
only when the selected signature does not require a member of that record
kind (P3, P5).

value.definition: Subject-described constraint judgments and operation outcomes map to the FOUNDATIONS core values satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis without raising standing. A refinement maps each value to exactly one core value. Operation stops include hold, gap, refusal(constraint) and refusal(basis), distinguished by cause and predicate.

grounding.quote:
Each constraint names its governed subject, predicate, judgment kind,
latitude and refusal (§3, Constraint). The judgment of a constraint
returns one value of the core result algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), directly or through a
refinement that the owning signature declares and that maps each of its
values to exactly one core value. Under the no-coercion rule of
FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result of a constraint follows that algebra and is never
coerced to satisfied (P5, P6). The
core values, the rule that no mapping raises a result's standing and the
boundary among out_of_frame, indeterminate and an evaluation that was not
performed are FOUNDATIONS §4 Results'. This law applies them to the
judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
member, and adds no core value.
